meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries and appraisals generated automatically from those abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are machine analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated. Read the source before acting clinically.
meta.appraisal_source: Automated critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Chen S, Gao Y, Liang Z, Zhang Y, Wang C et al.
articles.title: Effect of Kunxian capsule, a novel Tripterygium wilfordii preparation, on reducing proteinuria and slowing renal function decline in diabetic kidney disease: a 48-week randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: In an RCT of 80 DKD patients receiving irbesartan, adding Kunxian capsule increased 48-week proteinuria remission (57.50% vs. 25.00%) and reduced renal composite hard endpoints (10.00% vs. 32.50%) with a shorter median time to remission (5 months vs. not reached) and no difference in adverse events.

pico.intervention: Kunxian capsule plus standard therapy with irbesartan for 48 weeks
pico.comparison: Standard therapy with irbesartan alone for 48 weeks
pico.outcome: Proteinuria remission rate, degree of proteinuria reduction, median time to remission, slope of eGFR decline, incidence of renal composite hard endpoint, adverse events, and inflammatory markers

appraisal.bottom_line: Adding Kunxian capsule to irbesartan increased 48-week proteinuria remission (57.50% vs. 25.00%) and lowered the incidence of a renal composite hard endpoint (10.00% vs. 32.50%) without increasing adverse events in 80 DKD patients.
appraisal.relevance: Provides preliminary clinical evidence for an herbal preparation (Tripterygium wilfordii derivative) as an adjunctive therapy to RAS blockade for reducing proteinuria and eGFR decline in DKD.
appraisal.caveat: Small sample size (N=80), lack of reporting of exact 95% confidence intervals, p-values, eGFR slope estimates, or detailed hard endpoint definitions in the abstract.

articles.authors: Liu J, Wan JF, Chen J, Zhang WW, Peng CX et al.
articles.title: Risk factors for cognitive impairment in patients undergoing hemodialysis: an umbrella review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: An umbrella review of 5 meta-analyses (97 associations) identified multiple factors associated with cognitive impairment and frailty in hemodialysis patients, including higher education protective against cognitive impairment (OR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.13-0.34) and depression (OR = 4.66, 95% CI: 2.98-7.27), low-flux HD (OR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.97-8.79), stroke (OR = 2.94, 95% CI: 1.72-5.03), interdialytic hypotension (OR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.53-4.21), and longer HD duration (OR = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.49-3.53) linked to cognitive frailty.

pico.intervention: Risk factors including depression, stroke history, longer dialysis duration, low-flux hemodialysis, interdialytic hypotension, and demographic/clinical traits
pico.comparison: Absence of risk factors or protective factors such as higher educational attainment and higher serum albumin

inclusion: Meta-analyses evaluating factors associated with cognitive impairment or cognitive frailty in adult hemodialysis patients

appraisal.bottom_line: Multiple demographic, clinical, and dialysis-related factors are associated with cognitive impairment and frailty in maintenance hemodialysis patients, though the certainty of evidence for nearly all associations is low or very low.
appraisal.relevance: Identifies potentially modifiable dialysis prescriptions (such as low-flux dialyzers and interdialytic hypotension) and patient sub-populations for cognitive screening in HD units.
appraisal.caveat: Umbrella synthesis of observational evidence where association does not establish causality; only 2 of 97 evaluated associations possessed moderate-certainty evidence.

articles.authors: Pakkhesal S, Mohammadi P, Rezagholizadeh A, Koochaki Z, Ramezani MA et al.
articles.title: Proton pump inhibitors in prevention of cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity: a systematic review.
articles.summary: A systematic review of 8 studies (n=1062; 2 RCTs, 6 observational) found conflicting evidence on PPI co-administration during cisplatin chemotherapy, ranging from one RCT showing a non-significant trend toward protection (0% vs. 25% nephrotoxicity, p=0.078) to a cohort study showing increased AKI risk (OR = 2.78, p=0.010).

pico.intervention: Cisplatin therapy with proton pump inhibitor (PPI) co-administration
pico.outcome: Cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity, AKI incidence, post-treatment eGFR, and renal injury biomarkers

inclusion: RCTs and observational studies comparing cisplatin with PPI co-administration versus cisplatin without PPIs reporting renal outcomes

appraisal.bottom_line: Current evidence regarding PPI co-administration for preventing cisplatin nephrotoxicity is conflicting across 8 heterogeneous studies, yielding signals that range from modest protective trends to a significant risk of AKI (OR = 2.78, p=0.010).
appraisal.relevance: Cautions nephrologists and oncologists against using PPIs as a nephroprotective strategy during cisplatin treatment, given the potential signal for renal harm.
appraisal.caveat: High clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative meta-analysis; included studies were predominantly small observational cohorts subject to residual confounding.

articles.authors: Ahuja D, Concepcion BP, Yuan Y, Forbes R, Rogers JL et al.
articles.title: Transplantation of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Positive or Viremic Kidneys: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 6 studies comparing 638 recipients of HBV-positive kidneys with 2800 recipients of HBV-negative kidneys found similar allograft survival at 1 year (RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.98-1.01), 3 years (RR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.98-1.04), and 5 years (RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.91-1.09), alongside a low transmission rate (4.94%).

pico.intervention: Transplantation of kidneys from HBsAg-positive or viremic donors (n=638)
pico.comparison: Transplantation of kidneys from HBsAg-negative non-viremic donors (n=2800)
pico.outcome: Patient survival and allograft survival at 1, 3, and 5 years post-transplant, and HBV transmission rate

inclusion: Studies of recipients of HBsAg+ or viremic kidneys with a comparison group of HBV-negative donor kidney recipients reporting patient and graft survival

appraisal.bottom_line: Kidneys from HBV-infected donors demonstrate allograft and patient survival equivalent to HBV-negative kidneys up to 5 years post-transplant (5-year allograft RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.91-1.09) with low viral transmission rates (4.94%).
appraisal.relevance: Supports expanding the donor organ pool by safely utilizing HBV-positive kidneys in immune recipients under antiviral prophylaxis.
appraisal.caveat: Pooled analyses rely on observational cohort studies; explicit numerical effect sizes and confidence intervals for patient survival were omitted in the abstract, and long-term liver outcomes remain unassessed.

articles.authors: Wu Q, Yu Z, Lin X, Yang L, Wu Z
articles.title: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor across the kidney-cardiometabolic continuum: a systematic review.
articles.summary: A systematic review of 20 studies (n=31,416) found that elevated suPAR predicted incident CKD (adjusted OR = 3.13, 95% CI: 2.11-4.65) and ESKD (adjusted HR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.10-2.12) in adults with preserved baseline function, but offered minimal discriminative gain (C-statistic increase 0.027-0.08) and failed to differentiate FSGS from other glomerular diseases.

pico.population: Adults and pediatric patients across the kidney-cardiometabolic spectrum (n=31,416 across 20 studies)
pico.intervention: Elevated circulating soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) levels
pico.outcome: Incident CKD, ESKD, FSGS diagnostic discrimination, pediatric CKD progression, and cardiovascular outcomes

inclusion: Studies evaluating suPAR as a risk biomarker in CKD and cardiometabolic conditions searched through May 2026

appraisal.bottom_line: Although elevated suPAR independently predicts incident CKD (aOR = 3.13) and ESKD (aHR = 1.53) in adults with preserved kidney function, it provides trivial incremental discrimination (C-statistic gain <= 0.08) and cannot differentiate FSGS.
appraisal.relevance: Advises against routine clinical suPAR measurement in nephrology for risk stratification or primary FSGS diagnostic evaluation.
appraisal.caveat: Observational evidence base lacking decision curve analyses, lack of assay standardization, and loss of statistical independence after adjusting for baseline kidney function in pediatric and metabolic cohorts.

articles.authors: Liang C, Bao R, Yin S, Song T, Lin T
articles.title: Peri-transplant eculizumab for preventing antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplant recipients at high immunologic risk: a systematic review with design-stratified evidence synthesis.
articles.summary: A systematic review of peri-transplant eculizumab in high-immunologic-risk kidney transplantation found no reduction in centrally confirmed AMR in the only randomized trial (5/51 vs. 5/51; RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.31-3.25), despite historical cohort signals of benefit (RR = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.05-0.74).

pico.population: High-immunologic-risk kidney transplant recipients (sensitized, preformed DSA, or ABO-incompatible)
pico.comparison: Standard desensitization regimens or historical control protocols
pico.outcome: Antibody-mediated rejection (AMR), long-term graft survival, kidney function, persistent DSA, and chronic microvascular injury

inclusion: Studies evaluating peri-transplant eculizumab prophylaxis in high-immunologic-risk kidney transplantation

appraisal.bottom_line: Randomized evidence does not show that peri-transplant eculizumab lowers antibody-mediated rejection compared with standard desensitization alone (RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.31-3.25) or improves long-term graft survival.
appraisal.relevance: Indicates that routine addition of expensive terminal complement blockade with eculizumab is not supported by RCT evidence for incremental AMR reduction over standard protocols.
appraisal.caveat: Randomized evidence is restricted to a single small trial (N=102 total); historical cohort benefits (RR = 0.19) were strongly confounded by era changes in clinical management and plasma exchange.

articles.authors: Gong Y, Zheng J, Huang W, Jeon Y
articles.title: Comparative efficacy of different exercise modalities on renal function and glycemic control in patients with non-dialysis diabetic kidney disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A network meta-analysis of 20 RCTs (n=1,746) in non-dialysis DKD showed resistance training increased eGFR vs. usual care (MD = 11.36 mL/min/1.73 m², 95% CI: 4.47 to 18.25), mind-body exercise reduced UAE (SMD = -1.41, 95% CI: -2.67 to -0.16), and combined training lowered FBG persistently (MD = -1.71 mmol/L).

pico.population: Adults with non-dialysis diabetic kidney disease (20 RCTs, n=1,746)
pico.intervention: Structured exercise modalities (resistance, aerobic, combined, or mind-body) for >= 4 weeks
pico.outcome: eGFR, urinary albumin excretion (UAE), HbA1c, fasting blood glucose (FBG), and adverse events

inclusion: RCTs evaluating structured exercise (duration >= 4 weeks) vs. usual care or active comparator in non-dialysis DKD adults

appraisal.bottom_line: Combined exercise offers durable glycemic control (FBG MD = -1.71 mmol/L), mind-body exercise reduces albuminuria (SMD = -1.41), and resistance training's eGFR benefit (MD = 11.36) loses significance when high-risk trials are excluded.
appraisal.relevance: Provides evidence for tailoring specific exercise prescriptions to renal versus glycemic goals in non-dialysis DKD management.
appraisal.caveat: Low certainty of evidence across main outcomes, fragility of resistance training's eGFR benefit in sensitivity analyses, and poor safety monitoring (only 25% of trials reported adverse events).

articles.authors: Fernandes DCM, Gomide R, Magalhaes TR, de Sousa Lima RT, Silva RM et al.
articles.title: Biomarker-dependent detection of contrast-associated acute kidney injury after intra-arterial contrast procedures: an exploratory randomized trial.
articles.summary: In an exploratory single-blind RCT of 76 patients undergoing intra-arterial contrast procedures, creatinine-based criteria identified 4 CA-AKI cases while cystatin C-based criteria identified 7 additional cases, demonstrating poor diagnostic agreement (kappa = 0.07) and zero overlapping cases.

pico.population: Patients with peripheral arterial disease undergoing elective intra-arterial contrast-enhanced vascular procedures (n=76)
pico.intervention: Standardized hydration plus high-dose atorvastatin and N-acetylcysteine
pico.outcome: CA-AKI incidence defined by creatinine (>= 25% or >= 0.5 mg/dL increase within 72h) vs. cystatin C (>= 10% increase within 24h); diagnostic concordance

inclusion: Patients with peripheral arterial disease undergoing elective intra-arterial contrast-enhanced vascular procedures

appraisal.bottom_line: Creatinine- and cystatin C-based criteria for CA-AKI show near-zero diagnostic agreement (kappa = 0.07, 0 overlapping cases) after intra-arterial contrast, confirming that event detection is heavily biomarker-dependent.
appraisal.relevance: Highlights how endpoint selection profoundly alters event ascertainment and therapeutic effect estimates in clinical trials evaluating CA-AKI prevention.
appraisal.caveat: Small exploratory single-blind trial (N=76) with low overall event numbers (4 by creatinine, 7 by cystatin C), preventing definitive assessment of statin/NAC efficacy.

articles.authors: Rabiei L, Baharanchi FG, Nazari AM, Masoudi R
articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy versus group-based optimism training on psychological outcomes in hemodialysis patients: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: An 8-week RCT of 135 hemodialysis patients demonstrated that group-based optimism training yielded superior sustained improvements over CBT at 4-month follow-up for depression (Cohen's d = 0.45, p = 0.032) and optimism (d = 0.36, p = 0.041), while both interventions equally improved acute anxiety and hope.

pico.intervention: Cognitive behavioral therapy (8 sessions) OR Group-based optimism training (8 sessions)
pico.outcome: Anxiety, depression, optimism, and hope measured immediately post-intervention, 2 months, and 4 months later

appraisal.bottom_line: Both CBT and group optimism training reduce psychological distress versus control in HD patients, but optimism training produces superior long-term reductions in depression (d = 0.45, p = 0.032) at 4-month follow-up.
appraisal.relevance: Identifies group optimism training as an effective and potentially more durable non-pharmacological alternative to traditional CBT for treating depression in hemodialysis units.
appraisal.caveat: Trial was retrospectively registered and outcomes relied entirely on self-reported psychological instruments without blinded clinical diagnostic interviews.

articles.authors: An X, Geng J, Lei K, Su B
articles.title: Urinary kidney injury molecule-1 as a diagnostic biomarker for persistent severe acute kidney injury: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A Bayesian meta-analysis of 8 studies (n=2,349; 378 persistent severe AKI cases) showed uKIM-1 has moderate diagnostic performance for persistent severe AKI in adults, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.67 (95% CrI: 0.59-0.75), specificity of 0.73 (95% CrI: 0.61-0.84), DOR of 5.91 (95% CrI: 2.91-11.20), and AUC of 0.75 (95% CrI: 0.62-0.84).

pico.population: Adult patients across heterogeneous clinical settings (ICU, ED, postoperative, sepsis, COVID-19, liver transplant; n=2,349)
pico.comparison: Reference standard clinical definitions for persistent severe AKI
pico.outcome: Sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), area under the curve (AUC)

inclusion: Adult patient studies evaluating the diagnostic value of uKIM-1 for persistent severe AKI

appraisal.bottom_line: Urinary KIM-1 exhibits only moderate diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity 0.67, specificity 0.73, AUC 0.75) for detecting persistent severe AKI in adult patients.
appraisal.relevance: Demonstrates that uKIM-1 cannot be relied upon as a standalone diagnostic biomarker for persistent severe AKI in routine nephrology or critical care practice.
appraisal.caveat: Included studies spanned highly heterogeneous clinical settings (sepsis, liver transplant, post-op, COVID-19) with non-standardized diagnostic cutoff thresholds.
